doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Stuff's chemistry and Gordon Edwards's football analogy
summary: Everyone in Stuff respected each other's turf; Gordon Edwards likened the band to a football team and the members supported each other offstage.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: And you could say the same thing about the two guitarists. How can a group with two guitar players and two drummers and a bassist and multi-keyboardist not be busy? And well the proof was in the records I guess.

Yeah. Everybody in that group was very cognizant — to borrow your word — of what the other guy was playing and nobody was like suppressing their ego especially but everyone wanted — Gordon always equated it with a football team. You know everybody’s got a job to do, you’re the safety, you’re the center, he was the quarterback of course but this guy’s going out for a pass, this guy’s going to do blocking, this guy’s going to do a Hail Mary, all the football analogies really worked because that’s how the band worked. You know we really chose an area and made that our turf, individually. So Eric and Cornell never got in each other’s way, always complemented each other. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
Although each guy, you know, got solos. Same thing with Steve and I, we each got drum solos but when we were playing as a unit everybody was very respectful of the other guy’s turf. I’m sorry —

It was that way personally too, you know nobody interfered with anybody else’s offstage life but we were all supportive of each other in our offstage life and that really became exaggerated. Once we hit the stage we were totally supportive of each other.
